metadata.note: The Tampa Northern Railroad (incorporated 7 Apr 1906) built Tampa - Brooksville, 49 mi, the first leg of a planned Tampa - Atlanta line that never went further. Regular passenger trains from 4 Jun 1907 (contractor-operated until the end of 1907), first over the Brooksville & Hudson's old route north of Enville Jn via Wiscon, then from c.1909 over a new Enville Jn - Brooksville cut-off. The Seaboard Air Line bought the stock in July 1912 but the TN went on operating as an independent road; the SAL applied in Nov 1925 to lease/take trackage over it and ran it as its Brooksville Subdivision. SAL passenger service is confirmed to 1929 and was gone by 1934. Drawn: TN 1907-1908 on the original route, TN 1909-1925 and SAL 1926-1929 [OPEN] on the cut-off route (Rule 4 split at the c.1926 operator change, shared geometry). The south end is still CSX's Brooksville Subdivision; the line north of Broco Quarry was abandoned in the 1970s.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt), Table 44 and index

metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Seaboard Air Line: Brooksville Subdivision ends at 1929, the last CONFIRMED passenger year (Brooksville Journal 6 Jun 1929); the real end lies between 1929 and May 1934 ('for some years past' in Mar 1936 suggests c.1930-32). An SAL public timetable for 1930-1933 would settle it. (2) TN-to-SAL operator change drawn at 1926 (approximate): SAL's ICC application 28 Nov 1925; the ICC finance-docket decision was not found. (3) Passenger continuity 1913-1916, 1918-1924 and 1926-1928 is interpolated; a reported SAL 1926 timetable showing only freight on the subdivision was not checked. (4) Cut-over from the old Wiscon route to the Enville Jn - Brooksville cut-off: 1908 (West Pasco museum) vs c.1909 (Fowler); drawn 1908/1909. Where the old route rejoined (Loyce or Masaryktown) and the old route's length (OHM geometry 10.9 mi vs Fowler-implied 9.2) unresolved. (5) Opening: newspapers 4 Jun 1907 vs ICC formal openings 1 Oct 1907 / 1 Jan 1908 - newspapers used. (6) SAL control date: 1 Jul 1910 (West Pasco museum) vs Jul 1912 (Evening Star) - no operator change either way (ICC: TN operated its own trains to Dec 1917). (7) Headways and speeds after 1907 are estimates.
metadata.omitted: [3] Tooke Lake Branch (Tooke Lake Jn - Wiscon - Tooke Lake - Centralia, TN 1911-c.1926, SAL to 1930 abandonment): NOT DRAWN - no confirmable passenger year ('No passenger trains were running' in the 1930 ICC abandonment petition). Its grade is in OSM as old_railway_operator=SAL ways 1152008511-1152008521 and 53830138. [5] Brooksville & Hudson Railroad (predecessor, Brooksville - Fivay - Hudson, logging road, common carrier from 1904): NOT DRAWN - no dated passenger year. [6] Brooksville & Inverness (SAL, 1925): context only, not TN, no passenger year - NOT DRAWN.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Ex-TN line after the 1929-1934 passenger end (freight only; Feb 1952 Guide daggers at Fivay, Masaryktown); Tooke Lake Branch; Brooksville & Hudson west of Fivay Jn and its logging spurs; Hooker's Point / Tampa marine terminal trackage; CSX Brooksville Subdivision quarry trackage north of Brooksville. Rule 1.
metadata.ownership_split: TN 1907-1925 / SAL 1926-1929, split at the approximate c.1926 lease/trackage takeover (Rule 4). The July 1912 SAL stock purchase and 1917-1920 USRA control are NOT splits.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 48.6 mi Tampa Union Station - Brooksville. South of the junction near Masaryktown (chainage 38.4) this is the same CSX trace as the 1909-1925 feature (see its geometry_quality). NORTH OF THE JUNCTION this draws the ORIGINAL 1907-1908 Brooksville & Hudson alignment (report block [4]), not the later cut-off: it is OpenHistoricalMap way 201938235, which OHM labels 'Gainesville, Ocala, & Charlotte Harbor Railroad', start_date 1886 - that attribution looks wrong (the GO&CH is not known to have reached here), but the geometry is the route the report describes: west from Brooksville past Tooke Lake Jn to a turn near Wiscon (taken as Wiscon Jn, 28.5286 N -82.4415), then south toward Masaryktown. Its east-west stretch along 28.530 N is corroborated to within 0.3 km by OSM ways 1152008519, 1152008520, 1152008521 and 1152008511 (old_railway_operator=SAL, no railway tag: the later Tooke Lake Branch, which shared Tooke Lake Jn - Wiscon Jn with the old route); the north-south stretch has no independent OSM corroboration. The OHM way is a SKETCH, not a survey: 46 nodes over 9.9 mi, with chords of 1.75 mi (28.475-28.501 N) and 1.66 mi (along 28.530 N) and several of 0.5-0.7 mi. APPROXIMATED LEG: the OHM way ends 1.4 km (0.9 mi) west of the CSX line at 28.451 N -82.466; it is joined to the CSX line by a 0.9 mi straight line to the nearest point (28.4458 N -82.4529). Where the old route really rejoined (Enville Jn) is not established - Fowler is unsure whether at Loyce or Masaryktown. MILEAGE CONFLICT: junction - Brooksville on this geometry is 10.9 mi (incl. the 0.9 mi straight leg) vs 9.2 mi implied by Fowler's line-16 figures (Enville Jn 117 - Brooksville 107.8; report says 'about 11, not measured'), and the turn taken as Wiscon Jn lies 4.2 mi from the Brooksville end vs 2.2 mi in Fowler's figures (Wiscon Jn 110). Either Fowler's figures are on a different basis or the OHM grade swings further west than the B&H did; not resolved. Tampa end drawn into Union Station (not yet built: opened 1912); the 1907-1908 trains used TN's own depot near Twigg and Jefferson Sts, about 0.4 mi west - not drawn.

segments.note: Regular passenger service Tampa - Brooksville began Tuesday 4 June 1907: 'The first train on the regular schedule ... arrived here from Brooksville this morning ... Regular schedule will be maintained from this date' (Pensacola Journal 6 Jun 1907; Ocala Evening Star 5 Jun 1907, which calls the first train 'a mixed'; Gainesville Daily Sun 7 Jun 1907). The road was operated by the contractors Cullinane and Sisk until 31 Dec 1907 and by the Tampa Northern from 1 Jan 1908 (ICC valuation, which gives the formal openings as 1 Oct 1907 Tampa - Fivay Jn and 1 Jan 1908 Fivay Jn - Brooksville - the newspapers are the earlier primary evidence of trains carrying the public and are used; conflict recorded). Drawn on the ORIGINAL Brooksville & Hudson route north of Enville Jn (via Rural, Wiscon Jn, Tooke Lake Jn), bought by the TN in Oct 1907; 'Rural' is printed in a 1908 Official Guide (Fowler 1908G), so 1908 is the last year this route is confirmed. The new Enville Jn - Brooksville cut-off was built 1908 (West Pasco museum) / 'c.1909' (Fowler); exact cut-over not established, so 1908 stays on the old route and the cut-off is drawn from 1909. Headway is an estimate: one train each way daily, from the single schedule in the 1907 reports.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note carries the citation for its dates and service (research/branches/tampa_northern_railroad.txt blocks [1] and [4]); headway estimated from the 1907 opening reports, not from a timetable.

segments.note: Tampa Northern passenger service Tampa - Brooksville on the Enville Jn - Brooksville cut-off (built 1908 per West Pasco museum, 'c.1909' per Fowler; start year 1909 is the first year drawn on the new line, not a dated cut-over). Dated passenger evidence: 1911 a TN railway-mail clerk (The Caucasian / Dawson News, Apr 1911 - weak, RPO implies a passenger-carrying train); 15 May 1912 TN one of three tenant roads of the new Tampa Union Station (Washington Times); 1917 TN a tenant of Tampa Union Station Co. (ICC valuation); Dec 1925 the TN 'has been serving this local territory' (Fitzgerald Leader-Enterprise). Passenger years 1913-1916 and 1918-1924 are INTERPOLATED between these anchors; no dated TN timetable for 1913-1925 was found. The SAL bought the TN's stock in July 1912 but the TN 'will continue to operate as an independent road' (Evening Star 7 Jul 1912) - a stock purchase, not an operator change, so no colour split. USRA federal control 28 Dec 1917 - 29 Feb 1920 (ICC valuation) is not a company split in this repo. End 1925 = last year the TN is confirmed as the operating company; the SAL applied to the ICC on 28 Nov 1925 to lease/take trackage over the TN (Washington Times) - see the Seaboard Air Line feature. Headway is an estimate (one train each way daily), unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note carries the citation for its anchor years (1911, 1912, 1917, 1925); 1913-1916 and 1918-1924 are interpolated, and the 1909 start is the approximate cut-over year, not a dated event. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Seaboard Air Line passenger service over the former Tampa Northern, Tampa - Brooksville, as part of the SAL Brooksville Subdivision. START 1926 is the APPROXIMATE operator-change year: the SAL applied to the ICC on 28 Nov 1925 to acquire the TN 'through lease or trackage agreement' (Washington Times 28 Nov 1925); the ICC approval date and the date SAL crews first ran the trains were not found (bracket Dec 1925 - Jun 1929). A 'Seaboard passenger train northward bound' hit a car at the Spring Lake road crossing near Brooksville in late May / early June 1929 (Brooksville Journal 6 Jun 1929). [OPEN] Passenger service confirmed to 1929 by that report. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. By 24 May 1934 the SAL was only 'considering' establishing Brooksville - Tampa passenger service (Brooksville Journal), in Mar 1936 'for some years past there has been no passenger service by railroad to and through Brooksville' (Brooksville Sun) and still none in May 1937 (Brooksville Journal), so the end lies between 1929 and 1934. Do not extend without evidence. A secondary claim (chicagorailfan.com) of SAL passenger trains to Brooksville until the early 1940s conflicts with these three local primary reports and is not used. The Feb 1952 Official Guide marks Fivay and Masaryktown freight-only. Passenger years 1926-1928 are interpolated: an SAL 1926 timetable (cited by Wikipedia) reportedly mentions only freight on this subdivision - not checked, possibly a lapse. Headway is an estimate, unsourced.
